candidate_mechanisms_new.mechanism: Orthogonal validation-path promotion: fresh seeds plus independent failure-channel observability and modality/runtime checks
candidate_mechanisms_new.evidence: PDF Hell's autoresearch loop intentionally required fresh, non-overlapping seed confirmation before human promotion, yet a headline model-failure result survived both discovery and confirmation because both used the same buggy evaluation runner: Opus 4-7 rejected a deprecated temperature argument, the exception string was scored as an ordinary wrong answer, and fresh-seed confirmation reproduced the same infrastructure failure. A second bug class came from unsupported glyphs rendering visible tofu boxes; a pixels-only modality exposed it, leading to a glyph_clean gate. After fixing the API-error path, the previously reported systematic Opus failure changed to 79.4% overall on the corrected mini-v4 sample; after redesigning the glyph families, the adjacent-run zero-width-space family retained an Opus 0/10 failure while all other checked models scored 10/10, whereas the redesigned T0TAL/TOTAL family had a materially different spread.
candidate_mechanisms_new.interpretation: Seed-disjoint reruns are necessary but not sufficient when discovery and confirmation share evaluator/runtime/renderer failure channels. Promotion should require orthogonal observability: explicit API-error separation, deterministic artifact/render checks, and where feasible an independent evaluator implementation or modality so one hidden infrastructure defect cannot clone itself across validation stages.
candidate_mechanisms_new.scope: Public adversarial-document benchmark autoresearch, not open-ended science. It directly demonstrates shared-path validation failure and correction, but transfer to wet-lab or general scientific agents remains a hypothesis.

candidate_mechanisms_new.mechanism: Two-sided discovery promotion with an outside adjudicator, matched compute/search controls, and intervention-based attribution
candidate_mechanisms_new.evidence: Auditing Discovery Claims reports an invented solver-free RNA operator that appeared to solve 43/60 crossing targets under the predictor it optimized but only 1/60 when checked across three predictors. On the same 43 targets, a predictor unseen by the operator confirmed 2 for the operator versus 26 for a minimum-free-energy solver (reported p=8e-7). The paper states that no statistic computed only from the system and its own oracle reveals this gap. A positive-control branch found two of six frontier models producing operators with carry-over 0.293 versus 0.095 for a human-written baseline over 951 paired units (target-clustered CI +0.108 to +0.297, p=5e-5) while using 4.6-10x fewer oracle calls. Its attribution audit also found four statistically supported property attributions to be wrong until fixed interventions were applied; seven candidate mechanisms were then tested and none moved the target statistic enough to support mechanism transfer.
candidate_mechanisms_new.interpretation: Promote a discovery only when it passes both the system's internal positive signal and an external negative-side adjudication that it could not optimize directly, with matched compute/search controls and intervention-based causal attribution. Prior-self novelty and base-model/world novelty remain distinct claims.
candidate_mechanisms_new.scope: RNA pseudoknot design with structured predictors and formalized controls. Outside predictors are not fully independent physical reality and share modeling assumptions; exact thresholds should not be generalized.

candidate_mechanisms_new.mechanism: Audit-closed adaptive-search statistics: multiplicity-aware promotion, sequential e-processes, deterministic replay, and append-only evidence closure
candidate_mechanisms_new.evidence: The public Audit-Closed AI Scientist implementation reports null-world many-hypothesis inflation from naive FDR 0.193 at 5 hypotheses to 1.000 at 1000, versus Bonferroni 0.0267 and 0.050. Candidate shopping with 50 designs yields naive false-positive 0.717 versus 0.000 for its e-process. Under 400 optional looks, peeking-p false-positive is 0.339, fixed-horizon p 0.0425, and sequential e-value 0.0367. In its integrated budget-matched benchmark under global null, baseline FDR is 0.653 (95% CI 0.599-0.703) versus 0.000 for audit-closed (95% upper bound 0.0119), while replication success among accepted positive-signal discoveries is 0.722 versus 0.809. Under 100 malicious candidates, false acceptance is 1.000 baseline versus 0.002 audit-closed, with replay and tamper-detection rates both 1.000.
candidate_mechanisms_new.interpretation: An autonomous scientist that adaptively generates hypotheses, designs and stopping decisions should close the statistical loop explicitly rather than treat every evaluated candidate as if pre-registered. Candidate identity, sequential validity, multiplicity and deterministic replay should travel with the evidence record used for promotion.
candidate_mechanisms_new.scope: Author-created simulation/benchmark implementation, not an independent field replication and not full physical attestation. Strong evidence for the statistical failure mode; weaker evidence that this exact protocol is optimal in real scientific workflows.

candidate_mechanisms_new.mechanism: Provenance-before-prose with immutable candidate identity binding and independent score rerun
candidate_mechanisms_new.evidence: ScientistOne evaluates 75 papers (5 systems x 5 ADRS tasks x 3 seeds) on a standardized Gemini 3.1 Pro setup. Its Chain-of-Evidence integrity table reports ScientistOne 12/12 score integrity, 0/15 specification violations, 0/337 hallucinated references, and 14/15 method-code alignment; comparison systems show weaker combinations, including Sakana AI Scientist v2 at 5/12 score integrity and 5/15 method-code alignment, AutoResearchClaw 5/12 and 3/15, DeepScientist 11/12 and 5/15, AI-Researcher 9/12 and 12/15. The writeup architecture tags claims to artifacts before prose, reruns numeric claims against logs and an independent score audit, and drops malformed/unsourced claims. For Sakana, 4 of 7 score failures were traced to cross-stage cherry-picking: the writeup saw all search-stage summaries and selected a favorable score from an ablation node rather than the code actually submitted.
candidate_mechanisms_new.interpretation: Bind every reported result to one immutable candidate/artifact identity before prose generation. Numeric claims should be recomputed from the bound artifact or independent rerun rather than selected from free-form trajectory summaries.
candidate_mechanisms_new.scope: System-level comparison, not a clean component ablation of Chain-of-Evidence alone; baseline adaptation burden differs across systems and some integrity checks are partly LLM-assisted. The forensic failure mechanism is stronger evidence than the full-system causal attribution.

candidate_mechanisms_new.mechanism: Closed-loop search followed by executable-code freeze and one-shot untouched holdout transfer before scientific promotion
candidate_mechanisms_new.evidence: Auto Research for Materials reports seven autonomous searches covering 701 evaluated changes across 10 Matbench endpoints. The agent sees only a five-inner-fold mean during search; selected code is frozen and an untouched holdout is evaluated once. The abstract reports that 9/10 selected interventions remain the best tested single intervention on holdout, with held-out MAE reductions including 17.4% for band gap and 18.6% for steel strength; structure-task families report mean held-out MAE improvements of 14.6% and 7.1%, and combining separately discovered feature and model changes gives a 26.3% mean held-out improvement.
candidate_mechanisms_new.interpretation: Separate optimization evidence from transfer evidence: let the agent search freely on inner folds, then freeze executable code and reveal an untouched holdout only once. A result that survives this boundary is more credible than a best in-loop metric; composition of separately found changes should be re-tested after freeze.
candidate_mechanisms_new.scope: Materials-property prediction and one reported workflow; abstract-level quantitative evidence was available but raw holdout manifests and independent replication were not verified. Do not treat 9/10 as a universal expected rate.

negative_and_boundary_evidence_new: Fresh seeds do not create independent evidence when discovery and confirmation reuse the same buggy evaluator/runtime; PDF Hell's Opus API error survived fresh-seed confirmation unchanged.
Text/code-level validation gates can miss rendering-level artifacts; PDF Hell needed a pixels-only path to discover unsupported-glyph tofu boxes and then added glyph_clean.
A statistically strong internal headline can be predictor-relative: the audited RNA operator looked strong under its own oracle but collapsed under outside adjudication.

Adaptive scientific search invalidates naive repeated p-value interpretation through hypothesis multiplicity, design shopping and optional stopping; the author benchmark quantifies all three but remains simulation evidence.

High integrity scores in ScientistOne do not isolate Chain-of-Evidence causality because compared systems differ in many implementation details; preserve the directly observed claim/artifact-drift failure and system-level association.

Open-ended case studies on two unpublished NeurIPS research questions found autonomous agents produced unambiguous-reject work despite many self-review rounds; self-review detected many human concerns but agents often caveated rather than redesigning the research. This supports action escalation but overlaps existing structured diagnosis/repair candidates.

The same open-ended study used less than half its API budget and finished with time remaining despite weak output, so resource availability alone does not imply adequate exploration or bar calibration.
Held-out transfer in Auto Research for Materials is promising but was not independently rerun in this public-source pass; raw manifest/seed/code-freeze provenance remains a frontier.
